title: MIP 5053 (NSIC Rc 808H) Hybrid Rice: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: MIP 5053 (NSIC Rc 808H): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: MIP 5053 is NSIC Rc 808H, a hybrid rice for irrigated lowland: about 110 days and 8.7 tonnes per hectare on average. See its ratings.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 808H is a hybrid rice variety for irrigated lowland, sold as MIP 5053 and known locally as Mestiso 168. The NSIC approved it in 2026. Mahyco International Philippines bred it. It matures in about 110 days and averages 8.7 tonnes per hectare, with a top yield of 10.1 tonnes in trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for MIP 5053, or rice variety 808H, this is the one. The facts below come from sources that include PhilRice and its public seed database. So you can compare it with the other varieties in our [rice variety finder](/rice-varieties) before you buy seed. Also read our guide to [rice varieties in the Philippines](/crops/rice-varieties-philippines) for how inbreds, hybrids and special rice differ.

items: **Yield:** 8.7 tonnes per hectare on average, or about 174 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 10.1 tonnes.
**Watch out for:** green leafhopper, brown planthopper, stem borer, tungro.
**Cooked rice:** intermediate amylose, so soft but not sticky.

blocks.caption: From PhilRice's catalogue of released varieties (t/ha means tonnes per hectare)

blocks.text: How much does NSIC Rc 808H yield?

On average it gives 8.7 tonnes per hectare. That is about 174 cavans of 50 kilograms of palay. It sits above the average of the 180 irrigated lowland hybrids in PhilRice's list, which is 6.9 tonnes. But the top yield, 10.1 tonnes, came from a trial with good water, seed and care. So plan your costs on the average, then work toward the top with the habits in our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare).
How many days does it take to mature?

It takes about 110 days from sowing to harvest. IRRI groups varieties of 100 to 120 days as short duration and 120 to 140 days as medium, so this one counts as short duration. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow, as PalayCheck advises. Because the day count drives every task, anee.io counts it for you from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.

blocks.text: So scout early for [green leafhopper](/pests/green-leafhopper), [brown planthopper](/pests/brown-planthopper), [stem borer](/pests/rice-stem-borer), [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.

blocks.caption: Grain quality in PhilRice's seed database

blocks.text: Amylose decides how rice cooks. With intermediate amylose, expect rice that is soft but not sticky. In fact, PhilRice notes that Filipino taste moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer.

It suits irrigated lowland, where you control the water. Level the field well so the water stands evenly, and plant at the same time as your neighbors, one of the PalayCheck key checks, so pests cannot move from field to field. Our guide to [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation) shows each step. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: Is MIP 5053 the same as NSIC Rc 808H?
items.a: Yes. MIP 5053 is the name it is sold under, and NSIC Rc 808H is its registration with the National Seed Industry Council, where its local name is Mestiso 168. The numbers on this page are PhilRice's for NSIC Rc 808H.

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 808H?
items.a: It is known as Mestiso 168. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.

items.q: How many days does NSIC Rc 808H take to harvest?
items.a: About 110 days after sowing. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains are golden yellow.

items.q: What is the average yield of NSIC Rc 808H?
items.a: PhilRice lists 8.7 tonnes per hectare on average, about 174 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 10.1 tonnes. Your own yield depends on water, seed, fertilizer and timing.
Yes. So buy new seed each season, because seed saved from a hybrid crop does not grow true and yields less.

items.q: What should I watch for when I plant it?
items.a: In PhilRice's tests it was weak against green leafhopper, brown planthopper, stem borer, tungro. So scout from the early weeks and act at the first signs.
